title: Reading Drill — Preserving handwritten menus — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Preserving handwritten menus — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Ravensmere, work on faint prices being confused with later corrections had already produced a small collection of enlarged scans. The museum volunteer used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the rate of agreement between readers.

**B** The group kept paired transcription for the new trial, which was planned to run for seven weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that stains on the paper should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
